To help with both your **speaker return** and **laptop (17" → 13") change**, I first need to authenticate your account.

1) Please tell me your **email address** (the one you used at checkout).

Then, reply with:
2) The **order ID** for the speaker return (e.g., **#W0000000**).
3) The **order ID** for the laptop change (the one with the **17-inch** item).

After that, I’ll look up the orders, confirm the exact items/options involved, and tell you the exact steps (including asking for “yes” before I submit anything).

Fine, my email is aarav.santos8321@example.com. 

I don’t have the order IDs in front of me right now—can’t you just look them up by my email? I’ve only got one speaker and one 17-inch laptop order anyway. Don’t make this more complicated than it needs to be.
Error: User not found

I tried looking up your account by email, but I can’t find a matching user for **aarav.santos8321@example.com**.

2) Provide your **first name + last name + ZIP code** so I can look you up that way.

Are you kidding me? That’s the email I used. Whatever. My name is Aarav Santos and my ZIP code is 90017. Now hurry up and find my orders, I don’t have all day.

If you’d like, tell me the **city + state** on your order as well—then I can try a more accurate match.

Unbelievable. I have two emails—try aarav.santos8320@example.com this time. The name is spelled exactly as I gave it, and the ZIP is 90017. The city is Los Angeles, California. Now can you finally get this sorted?
